openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: The Inteno Pulse EX400 is a home desktop router supported by OpenWrt from version 24.10.1 onwards. The device is based on the MediaTek MT7621AT SoC and features 256 MB flash and 256 MB RAM. It offers dual-band WLAN, two 1 Gbit/s Ethernet ports and one USB 2.0 port. The Genexis Pulse EX400 is technically the same device.
openwrt_wiki.Installation OEM GUI: http://192.168.1.1 oder per DHCP am WAN; Login admin/admin; SYSTEM -> Firmware Upgrade -> Manual Firmware Upgrade, factory.bin; im Popup 'no'
openwrt_wiki.Installation OEM Recovery GUI: Press and hold the reset button by starting the device for about 10 seconds. Access the recovery web interface at http://192.168.1.1
openwrt_wiki.Hinweis Rückweg: Reverting to the original OEM firmware is not possible, as the manufacturer does not provide a downloadable OEM firmware image.
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: In the four corners of the bottom side are four screws under rubberstemps. After unscrewing these screws the top plate is held by some hooks at the middle of the side with the USB-Port and the opposite side. You can unlock these hooks by pushing the top plate and pulling the side plate with a screwdriver.
openwrt_wiki.Serial: 115200 Baud, 8N1, 3.3 V. The serial port is accessible from outside through two slots, each for two wires. The slots are left side of the WAN-port. Pinout: TX RX / VCC GND. You could leave VCC float.
openwrt_wiki.OEM Bootlog U-Boot: U-Boot 2016.09-rc2-g670ad7a (Sep 26 2020 - 23:43:16 +0200), Build: jenkins-gnxOS-Build-R-72; DRAM: 256 MiB; NAND: 256 MiB; DDR-1200Mhz, XTAL 40 MHz
openwrt_wiki.OEM Bootlog Kernel: Linux 4.4.14 (Image-Name 'MIPS OpenWrt Linux-4.4.93'), 'MIPS: machine is ex400', SoC MT7621 ver:1 eco:3, CPU MIPS 1004Kc, VPE topology {2,2}, nand: ESMT NAND 256MiB 3,3V 8-bit (Manufacturer ID 0xc8, Chip ID 0xda), SLC, erase size 128 KiB, page size 2048, OOB 64; mt7530-Switch; xhci-mtk; mt7603, mt7615 (MT7615E_EEPROM1.bin)

gluon_commit_touch.Text: The Genexis Pulse EX400 has a capacitive WPS button. This button is prone to errorous presses, as it is likely to be pressed when picking up or touching the device. The device in question has a recessed hardware reset switch for entering setup-mode. Ignore the capacitive touch button on the device in order to avoid unwanted activation of setup-mode.
